title: EPA proposal could leave the public in the dark on data center plans
summary:
The EPA proposal would eliminate a federal requirement that states notify the public and seek comment before issuing air pollution permits for data centers and other industrial facilities.
Critics say the move could thwart local residents from learning about proposed data centers or making their voices heard before projects are approved and construction begins.
The Republican president calls data centers critical to winning the AI race against China.
The federal plan would leave many communities in the dark before data centers show up in their backyards, they said.
Virginia and Georgia are both among states with the highest concentration of current and proposed data centers.

title: U.N. admits exceeding Paris Agreement’s 1.5-degree-C warming target is ‘unavoidable’
summary:
The world is set to blow past the Paris Agreement’s longtime threshold “within the next few years,” according to a new reportThe world is on track to exceed the Paris Agreement’s target of no more than 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming above preindustrial temperatures within the next few years, the United Nations admits in a new report.

Indeed, the U.S., the globe’s biggest historical greenhouse gas emitter, officially pulled out of the Paris Agreement in January.

title: 'Nothing but mud and silt' - the village swept away by deadly floods in Nepal
summary:
After the catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border a week ago, more than 1,000 people have died and nearly 4,000 more are missing, according to Nepal's disaster agency.
The BBC has travelled to the district of Betrawati in Nepal, as some people return to their homes to see the devastation caused by the floods.
South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri spoke to a local, who is still waiting for his his wife's body to be retrieved as rescue efforts continue.
More on this story.
